from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.",
            "Vector addition uses the tip-to-tail method.",
            "Scalar multiplication scales the arrow's length."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        # Visualize vector
        origin = np.array([1.5, -0.4, 0]) # Reference point for drawing
        v_vector = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = (2, 1.5)", color=WHITE).next_to(v_vector.get_end(), UP)
        
        self.play(Create(v_vector), Write(v_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        
        u_vector = Arrow(start=v_vector.get_end(), end=v_vector.get_end() + RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*0.5, color="#33FF57")
        u_label = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color="#33FF57").next_to(u_vector.get_midpoint(), RIGHT)
        sum_vector = Arrow(start=origin, end=u_vector.get_end(), color=YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Create(u_vector), Write(u_label))
        self.play(Create(sum_vector))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        
        # Scalar multiplication
        new_v = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + (RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5)*2, color="#3357FF")
        self.play(Transform(v_vector, new_v))
        self.play(FadeOut(u_vector), FadeOut(u_label), FadeOut(sum_vector))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: Redundancy", [
            "Linear dependence means having redundant vectors.", 
            "Redundant vectors don't add new dimensions.", 
            "Adding redundant vectors expands nothing."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display two vectors pointing in the same direction in #3357FF
        vec1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color="#3357FF")
        vec2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2.5, color="#3357FF")
        self.place_at_grid(vec1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(vec2, 'D3')
        self.play(Create(vec1), Create(vec2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3357FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate one vector fading out to show it's redundant
        self.play(FadeOut(vec2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the remaining vector as the essential direction
        self.play(vec1.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Bases: The Minimal Blueprint", [
            "A basis spans the entire space.",
            "Basis vectors are also linearly independent.",
            "A basis is the minimal blueprint required."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([1, -1], color=GREEN)
        v3 = Vector([2, 0], color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A basis spans the entire space.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2), FadeIn(v3))
        self.play(
            v1.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.5),
            v2.animate.shift(LEFT*0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Basis vectors are also linearly independent.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        # Highlight independence: shrink v3 as it is linear combination
        self.play(FadeOut(v3))
        self.play(Indicate(v1), Indicate(v2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A basis is the minimal blueprint required.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        basis_label = Text("Basis", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_label, "C4")
        self.play(Write(basis_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Visualization", [
            "Span defines our total reachable area.",
            "Linear dependence points out wasted effort.",
            "A basis is the efficient coordinate system."
        ])
        
        # Visualization objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        v1 = Vector([1, 0.5], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([0.5, 1], color=YELLOW)
        v3 = Vector([1.5, 1.5], color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.add(axes)
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(v3))
        self.play(v3.animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        grid_lines = VGroup(*[
            Line(axes.c2p(-3, i), axes.c2p(3, i), stroke_opacity=0.3) 
            for i in range(-3, 4)
        ], *[
            Line(axes.c2p(i, -3), axes.c2p(i, 3), stroke_opacity=0.3) 
            for i in range(-3, 4)
        ])
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as a directed line segment with magnitude and direction in 2D space. Visualize vector addition (tip-to-tail method) and scalar multiplication as scaling the arrow length.
sections.example: A robot arm on a 2D plane: Vector 'u' is the reach of segment 1, 'v' is segment 2. Their sum represents the robot's end-effector position.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Explain that a linear combination is a sum of scaled vectors (c1v1 + c2v2). 'Span' is the set of all reachable points. Visualize this as a 'coverage area' on a grid.
sections.example: If the robot arm moves only along vector 'u', its span is a line. If it uses 'u' and 'v', its span is the entire 2D plane.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
sections.content: Define linear dependence as having 'extra' vectors that don't add new dimensions to the span. If one vector can be formed by the others, it is redundant.
sections.example: Imagine three vectors pointing in the same direction. One vector is useful; the other two are redundant. The robot arm gains no new reach by adding them.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimal Blueprint
sections.content: Define a basis as a set of vectors that are linearly independent AND span the entire space. It is the 'minimal set' needed to describe any point in that space.
sections.example: In a 2D room, two perpendicular unit vectors (i and j) form a basis. Every point in the room can be uniquely identified by their combination.

sections.title: Summary and Visualization
sections.content: Recap: Span (reach), Linear Dependence (redundancy), and Basis (the coordinate system). Emphasize that a basis is the most efficient language for a space.
sections.example: Final Animation: An empty grid transforms as we add vectors; first a line (dependent), then a plane (spanning/basis). The grid lines shift to align with the chosen basis vectors.
